studies.Reference: Large prospective investigation of meat intake, related mutagens, and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
studies.Title: Large prospective investigation of meat intake, related mutagens, and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
studies.Authors: Daniel CR, Cross AJ, Graubard BI, Park Y, Ward MH, Rothman N, Hollenbeck AR, Chow WH, Sinha R
studies.Journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
studies.Population: NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study subcohort

sample_size.excerpt: After the exclusions, the baseline analytic cohort included 492,186 ( n = 293,466 men and 198,720 women) participants. The analysis of compounds in cooked and processed meats was restricted to a subcohort that responded to the second questionnaire and met the inclusion criteria above ( n = 302,162; 176,179 men and 125,983 women).

cases.excerpt: Over a mean follow-up of 9 y, we ascertained 1814 cases of RCC ( n = 498 clear cell; n = 115 papillary cell; n = 1071 NOS; n = 147 otherwise specified) in the baseline analysis and 1,089 cases of RCC ( n = 306 clear cell; n = 83 papillary cell; n = 617 NOS; n = 90, otherwise specified) in the subcohort analysis.

confidence_interval.excerpt: For participants in the highest compared with the lowest quintiles of total red meat intake, we observed a tendency toward an increased risk of total RCC (HR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.01, 1.40; P -trend = 0.06).

p_value.excerpt: We observed a positive trend for heme iron intake and total RCC ( P -trend = 0.03)

comparison.excerpt: HRs, 95% CIs, and P values for linear trend (using the median value within quintiles) are reported across sex-specific quintiles of intake with the lowest intake quintile representing the referent group.

design.excerpt: The NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study is a large prospective cohort of US men and women, aged 50–71 y, residing in 6 states (California, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania) and 2 metropolitan areas (Atlanta, GA, and Detroit, MI).

timing.excerpt: In a large US cohort, we prospectively investigated intake of meat and meat-related compounds in relation to risk of RCC, as well as clear cell and papillary RCC histologic subtypes.

continent.excerpt: The NIH-AARP Diet and Health Study is a large prospective cohort of US men and women, aged 50–71 y, residing in 6 states (California, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania) and 2 metropolitan areas (Atlanta, GA, and Detroit, MI).

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Meat intake, cooking method, and degree of doneness were linked to the Computerized Heterocyclic Amines Resource for Research In Epidemiology of Disease (CHARRED) database ( http://charred.cancer.gov/ ) to estimate values (ng/d) of 3 HCAs (PhIP, MeIQx, and DiMeIQx), one PAH (BaP), and heme iron by using an exposure index described in detail elsewhere ( 22 , 23 ).

gender.excerpt: The analysis of compounds in cooked and processed meats was restricted to a subcohort that responded to the second questionnaire and met the inclusion criteria above ( n = 302,162; 176,179 men and 125,983 women).
